title: Check the caller contract and owner lifetime before repairing a helper
applies_when: Descriptor/global, identity/cache, self-comparison, field-loss or cleanup claims omit caller, helper or result assembly.
lesson: Trace caller, descriptors, __main__, platform predicates, strong references/invalidation, cleanup/reset and ordered result assembly. Skipping a spread need not remove ...result fields. Check empty/nonempty and success controls. SDK cancellation can leave outer retries alive. Failed upload Writers need abort via an upload-owned context, preserving caller authority and successful Close. Admission guards may allow lifecycle work that clears pending state before final verification. Invented APIs are feature changes; profile matching is not topology support. Choose the next check, not blanket rejection.
avoid_when: Public helpers may fail without shipped callers. Strong references do not prevent mutation, stale metadata or concurrency bugs. Cleanup tests cover reached scenarios only. Spreads preserve present enumerable properties, not later overwrites or producer changes. Upload abort must not close caller-owned successful streams. SDK stack checks are revision-bound; no accelerator performance or general false-positive rate is established.

evidence.note: v7.26.8 requires x-reqid/x-log, otherwise ErrMaliciousResponse. Plain200/JSON is not SDK success; fix fixtures, not validation.

Real GCS SDK/local HTTP: Reader errors leak Writer monitors; child cancellation aborts without partial commit or caller cancellation. Empty/small/multi-chunk success controls pass. Native/race uses an SDK-internal frame, not live GCS or throughput.

Rejecting a second session's hooks does not revoke its admitted request. Native revocation/one-shot-ack controls do not cover service restarts/all timelines.

Real S3 SDK cancellation does not stop ListAll's outer retry. Cancel/deadline/backoff and transient 503 recovery controls check producer lifetime. Native/race covers draining receivers and nil failure sentinel, not blocked consumers, token recovery, delimiter/sharded paths, all backends or performance.
Closed/unmerged prior work covers retry cancellation, token recovery/backoff. No novelty or broader-patch qualification from the narrow test.
The 2026.8.1 exception admits lifecycle, not final validation. Recollecting errors after their cause is cleared is not resurrection.
Completion promotes legacy state, runs pre/postinstall, then rejects pending markers. Nine native interruption/retry cases, not published-package/full-CLI proof.
